newsitem.title: USA: Insteel sees ongoing start-up costs.
newsitem.headline: Insteel sees ongoing start-up costs.

text.p: Wire products producer Insteel Industries Inc said on Thursday that start-up costs at its Virginia facilty would continue to affect earnings performances until the first fiscal quarter of 1998.
The costs involve the expansion of the facility and the launching of tire bead wire production there.
"Although we are behind schedule due to construction and equipment start-up delays, most of these problems are behind us," said Insteel president and chief executive H.O. Woltz III.

"Pre-operating costs reduced third quarter earnings by approximately seven cents a share," he continued. "We anticipate that Virginia start-up costs will continue to affect our financial performance until sales ramp up to significant levels in the first fiscal quarter of 1998."
The company added that it expected to generate its first bead and welding wire revenues during the current quarter.
The company reported third quarter earnings from continuing operations of $1.2 million, or $0.14 per share, a decline from $2.4 million, or $0.29 per share, for the same period last year.
